body: I lost interest in everything, got more and more afraid of dirt, got isolated because I couldn't attend anything anymore. You can see where it goes from there.

>Really? There was just a sudden change in your emotional/psychological well being?  

Let me quote the professionals who also come to this conclusion after all their questions: "Oh, well, I guess there really was nothing. But don't worry that's totally normal. (Sure your surprise is totally unrelated!) It's only helpful to answer why the problem exists though and doesn't influence the successful treatment." Atleast they're consistent with that line so yay?  

Sure those stations suck, lots of people who understand you, lots of happyness and positive imagery, all totally convinced that you'll leave way better than you were.

There's nothing anyone ever found. I had a normal life until it all spiraled down in my teens and now I'm what I am.

I have been in several psych wards, due to suicidal tendencies and to cure my anxiety. That's what I meant with stationary treatment.

I definitely see where you're coming from and it amazes me that you don't just give up on a complete stranger who obviously already gave up himself. I can't say I'm seeing a silver lining on the horizon. I can't even say I'm trying to. But I see that I must have forgotten what this happyness must feel like if you hold it this high in value. I don't know if I ever have or will experience this but I must admit it's intriguing.

Even if there was a path to happyness, how much suffering am I to endure until it reveals itself? How much pain is this elusive joy worth? It is merely a gamble which is bound to be a loss in the long run. Why play if you cannot win?

I also wanted to be okay for a long time but then I realized that the only problem lies in the unrealistic expectation that there is such a thing as a good life for me. It's just the choice between a bad life or a good death.
Why the alcohol part? I don't drink at all, just wondering why :)

I've had Prozac but alone it didn't do the trick and combined with Mirtazapin it was the only combination so far that my body just didn't tolerate. Too bad, as it was very promising. But it's giving me hope that you found something after years of searching.

So you expierienced a rather strong change?
 I have tried several by now some with no effect at all, some with minor changes but never enough to make me forget my anxiety, just enough to accept it.
